title: Car-GPT: Could LLMs finally make self-driving cars happen?
title_zh: 自动驾驶汽车的突破可能像青霉素的发现一样偶然

paragraphs.en: In 1928, London was in the middle of a terrible health crisis, devastated by bacterial diseases like pneumonia, tuberculosis, and meningitis. Confined in sterile laboratories, scientists and doctors were stuck in a relentless cycle of trial and error, using traditional medical approaches to solve complex problems.
paragraphs.zh: 1928年，伦敦正处于一场可怕的公共卫生危机之中，肺炎、结核病和脑膜炎等细菌性疾病使这座城市饱受摧残。 被困在无菌实验室里的科学家和医生们陷入了无休止的试错循环，试图用传统的医学方法解决复杂的问题。

sents.en: In 1928, London was in the middle of a terrible health crisis, devastated by bacterial diseases like pneumonia, tuberculosis, and meningitis.
sents.zh: 1928年，伦敦正处于一场可怕的公共卫生危机之中，肺炎、结核病和脑膜炎等细菌性疾病使这座城市饱受摧残。

sents.en: Confined in sterile laboratories, scientists and doctors were stuck in a relentless cycle of trial and error, using traditional medical approaches to solve complex problems.
sents.zh: 被困在无菌实验室里的科学家和医生们陷入了无休止的试错循环，试图用传统的医学方法解决复杂的问题。

paragraphs.en: This is when, in September 1928, an accidental event changed the course of the world. A Scottish doctor named Alexander Fleming forgot to close a petri dish (the transparent circular box you used in science class), which got contaminated by mold. This is when Fleming noticed something peculiar: all bacteria close to the moisture were dead, while the others survived.
paragraphs.zh: 就是在1928年9月，一个偶然事件改变了世界的进程。 一位名叫亚历山大·弗莱明的苏格兰医生忘记盖上一个培养皿（就是你在科学课上用过的那种透明圆形盒子），结果它被霉菌污染了。 这时弗莱明注意到了一件奇怪的事：靠近潮湿处的细菌全都死了，而其他的细菌则存活了下来。

sents.en: This is when, in September 1928, an accidental event changed the course of the world.
sents.zh: 就是在1928年9月，一个偶然事件改变了世界的进程。

sents.en: A Scottish doctor named Alexander Fleming forgot to close a petri dish (the transparent circular box you used in science class), which got contaminated by mold.
sents.zh: 一位名叫亚历山大·弗莱明的苏格兰医生忘记盖上一个培养皿（就是你在科学课上用过的那种透明圆形盒子），结果它被霉菌污染了。

sents.en: This is when Fleming noticed something peculiar: all bacteria close to the moisture were dead, while the others survived.
sents.zh: 这时弗莱明注意到了一件奇怪的事：靠近潮湿处的细菌全都死了，而其他的细菌则存活了下来。

paragraphs.en: "What was that moisture made of?" wondered M. Flemming. This was when he discovered that Penicillin, the main component of the mold, was a powerful bacterial killer. This led to the groundbreaking discovery of penicillin, leading to the antibiotics we use today. In a world where doctors were relying on existing well-studied approaches, Penicillin was the unexpected answer.
paragraphs.zh: “那些水分是由什么构成的？”弗莱明（M. Flemming）感到好奇。 正是在那时，他发现青霉菌的主要成分青霉素是一种强大的细菌杀手。 这促成了青霉素这一突破性的发现，进而带来了我们今天使用的抗生素。 在医生们都依赖现有成熟方法的时代，青霉素是一个意想不到的答案。

sents.en: "What was that moisture made of?" wondered M. Flemming.
sents.zh: “那些水分是由什么构成的？”弗莱明（M. Flemming）感到好奇。

sents.en: This was when he discovered that Penicillin, the main component of the mold, was a powerful bacterial killer.
sents.zh: 正是在那时，他发现青霉菌的主要成分青霉素是一种强大的细菌杀手。

sents.en: This led to the groundbreaking discovery of penicillin, leading to the antibiotics we use today.
sents.zh: 这促成了青霉素这一突破性的发现，进而带来了我们今天使用的抗生素。

sents.en: In a world where doctors were relying on existing well-studied approaches, Penicillin was the unexpected answer.
sents.zh: 在医生们都依赖现有成熟方法的时代，青霉素是一个意想不到的答案。

paragraphs.en: Self-driving cars may be following a similar event. Back in the 2010s, most of them were built using what we call a « modular » approach. The software « autonomous » part is split into several modules, such as Perception (the task of seeing the world), or Localization (the task of accurately localize yourself in the world), or Planning (the task of creating a trajectory for the car to follow, and implementing the « brain » of the car). Finally, all these go to the last module: Control, that generates commands such as « steer 20° right », etc… So this was the well-known approach.
paragraphs.zh: 自动驾驶汽车可能正在经历一个类似的事件。 回到2010年代，它们中的大多数都是采用我们所谓的「模块化」方法构建的。 软件的「自主」部分被拆分成多个模块，例如感知（观察世界的任务）、定位（在世界中精确定位自身位置的任务）或规划（为汽车创建行驶轨迹的任务，相当于实现汽车的「大脑」）。 最后，所有这些都会传递到最后一个模块：控制，它生成诸如「向右转向20°」之类的命令等等。这就是众所周知的经典方法。

sents.en: Self-driving cars may be following a similar event.
sents.zh: 自动驾驶汽车可能正在经历一个类似的事件。

sents.en: Back in the 2010s, most of them were built using what we call a « modular » approach.
sents.zh: 回到2010年代，它们中的大多数都是采用我们所谓的「模块化」方法构建的。

sents.en: The software « autonomous » part is split into several modules, such as Perception (the task of seeing the world), or Localization (the task of accurately localize yourself in the world), or Planning (the task of creating a trajectory for the car to follow, and implementing the « brain » of the car).
sents.zh: 软件的「自主」部分被拆分成多个模块，例如感知（观察世界的任务）、定位（在世界中精确定位自身位置的任务）或规划（为汽车创建行驶轨迹的任务，相当于实现汽车的「大脑」）。

sents.en: Finally, all these go to the last module: Control, that generates commands such as « steer 20° right », etc… So this was the well-known approach.
sents.zh: 最后，所有这些都会传递到最后一个模块：控制，它生成诸如「向右转向20°」之类的命令等等。这就是众所周知的经典方法。

paragraphs.en: But a decade later, companies started to take another discipline very seriously: End-To-End learning . The core idea is to replace every module with a single neural network predicting steering and acceleration, but as you can imagine, this introduces a black box problem.
paragraphs.zh: 但十年后，各公司开始非常认真地对待另一门学科：端到端学习。 其核心思想是用一个单一的神经网络来替换所有模块，以预测转向和加速，但可以想象，这会带来黑箱问题。

sents.en: But a decade later, companies started to take another discipline very seriously: End-To-End learning .
sents.zh: 但十年后，各公司开始非常认真地对待另一门学科：端到端学习。

sents.en: The core idea is to replace every module with a single neural network predicting steering and acceleration, but as you can imagine, this introduces a black box problem.
sents.zh: 其核心思想是用一个单一的神经网络来替换所有模块，以预测转向和加速，但可以想象，这会带来黑箱问题。

paragraphs.en: These approaches are known, but don’t solve the self-driving problem yet. So, we could be wondering: "What if LLMs (Large Language Models), currently revolutionizing the world, were the unexpected answer to autonomous driving?"
paragraphs.zh: 这些方法是已知的，但尚未解决自动驾驶问题。 于是，我们可能会好奇：“如果目前正在颠覆世界的大语言模型（LLMs），恰恰是自动驾驶出乎意料的答案，会怎样呢？”

sents.en: These approaches are known, but don’t solve the self-driving problem yet.
sents.zh: 这些方法是已知的，但尚未解决自动驾驶问题。

sents.en: So, we could be wondering: "What if LLMs (Large Language Models), currently revolutionizing the world, were the unexpected answer to autonomous driving?"
sents.zh: 于是，我们可能会好奇：“如果目前正在颠覆世界的大语言模型（LLMs），恰恰是自动驾驶出乎意料的答案，会怎样呢？”

paragraphs.en: This is what we're going to see in this article, beginning with a simple explanation of what LLMs are and then diving into how they could benefit autonomous driving.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是我们将在本文中看到的内容，首先简单解释一下什么是 LLM，然后深入探讨它们如何为自动驾驶带来益处。

paragraphs.en: Before you read this article, you must know something: I'm not an LLM pro, at all. This means, I know too well the struggle to learn it. I understand what it's like to google "learn LLM"; then see 3 sponsored posts asking you to download e-books (in which nothing concrete appears)... then see 20 ultimate roadmaps and GitHub repos, where step 1/54 is to view a 2-hour long video (and no one knows what step 54 is because it's so looooooooong).
paragraphs.zh: 在阅读本文之前，你必须了解一点：我完全不是大语言模型专家。 这意味着，我非常清楚学习它的艰辛。 我明白那种感觉：搜索“学习大语言模型”，然后看到 3 条让你下载电子书的推广帖（其中没有任何具体内容）……接着又看到 20 份“终极路线图”和 GitHub 仓库，其中第 1 步（共 54 步）是观看一个长达 2 小时的视频（而且没人知道第 54 步是什么，因为清单实在太——长了）。

paragraphs.en: So, instead of putting you through this pain myself, let's just break down what LLMs are in 3 key ideas:
paragraphs.zh: 所以，与其让你亲自经历这种痛苦，不如让我们用 3 个关键思想来拆解大语言模型（LLM）到底是什么：

paragraphs.en: In ChatGPT, you input a piece of text, and it returns text, right? Well, what's actually happening is that your text is first converted into tokens.
paragraphs.zh: 在 ChatGPT 中，你输入一段文本，它会返回文本，对吧？ 实际上发生的事情是，你的文本会先被转换成词元（tokens）。

sents.en: In ChatGPT, you input a piece of text, and it returns text, right?
sents.zh: 在 ChatGPT 中，你输入一段文本，它会返回文本，对吧？

sents.en: Well, what's actually happening is that your text is first converted into tokens.
sents.zh: 实际上发生的事情是，你的文本会先被转换成词元（tokens）。

paragraphs.en: But what's a token? You might ask. Well, a token can correspond to a word, a character, or anything we want. Think about it -- if you are to send a sentence to a neural network, you didn't plan on sending actual words, did you?
paragraphs.zh: 但什么是词元？你可能会问。 其实，一个词元可以对应一个词、一个字符，或者任何我们想要的东西。 想一想——如果你要把一个句子发送给神经网络，你并不打算发送真实的词，对吧？

sents.en: But what's a token? You might ask.
sents.zh: 但什么是词元？你可能会问。

sents.en: Well, a token can correspond to a word, a character, or anything we want.
sents.zh: 其实，一个词元可以对应一个词、一个字符，或者任何我们想要的东西。

sents.en: Think about it -- if you are to send a sentence to a neural network, you didn't plan on sending actual words, did you?
sents.zh: 想一想——如果你要把一个句子发送给神经网络，你并不打算发送真实的词，对吧？

paragraphs.en: The input of a neural network is always a number, so you need to convert your text into numbers; this is tokenization.
paragraphs.zh: 神经网络的输入始终是数字，因此你需要将文本转换为数字，这就是分词（tokenization）。

paragraphs.en: Depending on the model (ChatGPT, LLAMA, etc...), a token can mean different things: a word, a subword, or even a character. We could take the English vocabulary and define these as words or take parts of words (subwords) and handle even more complex inputs. For example, the word « a » could be token 1, and the word « abracadabra » would be token 121.
paragraphs.zh: 取决于具体的模型（ChatGPT、LLAMA 等），token 可以有不同的含义：一个词、一个子词，甚至一个字符。 我们可以采用英语词汇表，把这些定义为词，或者取词的一部分（子词），从而处理更复杂的输入。 例如，词「a」可以是 token 1，而词「abracadabra」则是 token 121。

sents.en: Depending on the model (ChatGPT, LLAMA, etc...), a token can mean different things: a word, a subword, or even a character.

paragraphs.en: If you start looking around, you will see that some models are based on an encoder-decoder architecture, some others are purely encoder-based, and others, like GPT, are purely decoder-based.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你开始四处观察，你会发现有些模型基于编码器-解码器架构，有些纯粹基于编码器，还有一些，比如 GPT，则纯粹基于解码器。

paragraphs.en: Whatever the case, they all share the core Transformer blocks: multi-head attention, layer normalization, addition and concatenation, blocks, cross-attention, etc...
paragraphs.zh: 无论如何，它们都共享核心的 Transformer 模块：多头注意力、层归一化、相加与拼接、模块、交叉注意力等等……

paragraphs.en: In this model, multi-view images are sent to an Encoder-Decoder network that is trained to predict annotations of objects such as bounding boxes, and attention maps). These maps are then combined with a prompt like 'find the vehicles that are turning right'.The next block then finds the 3D Bounding Box localization and assigns IDs using a bipartite graph matching algorithm like the Hungarian Algorithm .
paragraphs.zh: 在该模型中，多视角图像被发送到一个编码器-解码器（Encoder-Decoder）网络，该网络经过训练可预测物体的标注，例如边界框和注意力图。 这些图随后与诸如「找出正在右转的车辆」之类的提示结合，接下来的模块随后利用二分图匹配算法（如匈牙利算法）进行三维边界框定位并分配 ID。

sents.en: These maps are then combined with a prompt like 'find the vehicles that are turning right'.The next block then finds the 3D Bounding Box localization and assigns IDs using a bipartite graph matching algorithm like the Hungarian Algorithm .

paragraphs.zh: 这很酷，但这并不是目前为止大语言模型「最好」的应用：

paragraphs.en: If Chat-GPT can find objects in an image, it should be able to tell you what to do with these objects, shouldn't it? Well, this is the task of Planning i.e. defining a path from A to B, based on the current perception. While there are numerous models developed for this task, the one that stood out to me was Talk2BEV :
paragraphs.zh: 如果 Chat-GPT 能够在图像中找到物体，那它应该也能告诉你如何处理这些物体，对吧？ 这就是规划（Planning）任务，即基于当前的感知结果定义一条从 A 到 B 的路径。 虽然针对这一任务已经开发了许多模型，但令我印象深刻的是 Talk2BEV：

sents.en: Well, this is the task of Planning i.e. defining a path from A to B, based on the current perception.
sents.zh: 这就是规划（Planning）任务，即基于当前的感知结果定义一条从 A 到 B 的路径。

sents.en: While there are numerous models developed for this task, the one that stood out to me was Talk2BEV :
sents.zh: 虽然针对这一任务已经开发了许多模型，但令我印象深刻的是 Talk2BEV：

paragraphs.en: The main difference between models for planning and Perception-only models is that here, we're going to train the model on human behavior to suggest ideal driving decisions. We're also going to change the input from multi-view to Bird Eye View since it is much easier to understand.
paragraphs.zh: 用于规划的模型与仅感知模型的主要区别在于，在这里，我们将通过人类行为来训练模型，以建议理想的驾驶决策。 我们还将把输入从多视角改为鸟瞰图，因为鸟瞰图更容易理解。

sents.en: The main difference between models for planning and Perception-only models is that here, we're going to train the model on human behavior to suggest ideal driving decisions.
sents.zh: 用于规划的模型与仅感知模型的主要区别在于，在这里，我们将通过人类行为来训练模型，以建议理想的驾驶决策。

sents.en: We're also going to change the input from multi-view to Bird Eye View since it is much easier to understand.
sents.zh: 我们还将把输入从多视角改为鸟瞰图，因为鸟瞰图更容易理解。

paragraphs.en: This model works both with LLaVA and ChatGPT4, and here is a demo of the architecture:
paragraphs.zh: 该模型同时适用于 LLaVA 和 ChatGPT4，以下是该架构的演示：

paragraphs.en: As you can see, this isn't purely "prompt" based, because the core object detection model stays Bird Eye View Perception, but the LLM is used to "enhance" that output by suggesting to crop some regions, look at specific places, and predict a path. We're talking about "language enhanced BEV Maps".
paragraphs.zh: 如你所见，这并非纯粹基于「提示词」，因为核心的目标检测模型仍然是鸟瞰图感知，但大语言模型被用来「增强」该输出，例如建议裁剪某些区域、关注特定位置，以及预测路径。 我们讨论的是「语言增强的鸟瞰图地图」。

sents.en: As you can see, this isn't purely "prompt" based, because the core object detection model stays Bird Eye View Perception, but the LLM is used to "enhance" that output by suggesting to crop some regions, look at specific places, and predict a path.

sents.en: We're talking about "language enhanced BEV Maps".
sents.zh: 我们讨论的是「语言增强的鸟瞰图地图」。

paragraphs.en: Other models like DriveGPT are trained to send the output of Perception to Chat-GPT and finetune it to output the driving trajectory directly.
paragraphs.zh: 其他模型如 DriveGPT 则被训练为将感知的输出发送给 ChatGPT，并对其进行微调，使其直接输出驾驶轨迹。

paragraphs.en: The architecture takes images, actions, and text prompts as input, and then uses a World Model (an understanding of the world and its interactions) to produce a video.
paragraphs.zh: 该架构以图像、动作和文本提示作为输入，然后使用世界模型（对世界及其交互的理解）来生成视频。

paragraphs.en: You can find more examples on Wayve's YouTube channel and this dedicated post .
paragraphs.zh: 您可以在 Wayve 的 YouTube 频道和这篇专门的文章中找到更多示例。

paragraphs.en: Similarly, you can see MagicDrive , which takes the output of Perception as input and uses that to generate scenes:
paragraphs.zh: 同样，你可以看到 MagicDrive，它将感知（Perception）的输出作为输入，并用其来生成场景：

paragraphs.en: Other models, like Driving Into the Future and Driving Diffusion can directly generate future scenarios based on the current ones. You get the point; we can generate scenes in an infinite way, get more data for our models, and have this endless positive loop.
paragraphs.zh: 其他模型，例如 Driving Into the Future 和 Driving Diffusion，可以直接基于当前场景生成未来场景。 你明白了这个道理：我们可以以无限的方式生成场景，为我们的模型获取更多数据，并形成这种无尽的正向循环。

sents.en: Other models, like Driving Into the Future and Driving Diffusion can directly generate future scenarios based on the current ones.
sents.zh: 其他模型，例如 Driving Into the Future 和 Driving Diffusion，可以直接基于当前场景生成未来场景。

sents.en: You get the point; we can generate scenes in an infinite way, get more data for our models, and have this endless positive loop.
sents.zh: 你明白了这个道理：我们可以以无限的方式生成场景，为我们的模型获取更多数据，并形成这种无尽的正向循环。

paragraphs.en: We've just seen 3 prominent families of LLM usage in self-driving cars: Perception, Planning, and Generation. The real question is...
paragraphs.zh: 我们刚刚了解了自动驾驶汽车中大语言模型应用的三大主要方向：感知、规划和生成。真正的问题是……

paragraphs.en: And by this, I mean... What if your model has hallucinations? What if its replies are completely absurd, like ChatGPT sometimes does? I remember, back in my first days in autonomous driving, big groups were already skeptical about Deep Learning, because it wasn't "deterministic" (as they call it).
paragraphs.zh: 我的意思是…… 如果你的模型出现幻觉怎么办？ 如果它的回复完全荒谬，就像 ChatGPT 有时会那样，怎么办？ 我记得，在我刚进入自动驾驶领域的那段时间，一些大团队已经对深度学习持怀疑态度，因为它不是他们所说的“确定性”的。

sents.en: And by this, I mean...
sents.zh: 我的意思是……

sents.en: What if your model has hallucinations?
sents.zh: 如果你的模型出现幻觉怎么办？

sents.en: I remember, back in my first days in autonomous driving, big groups were already skeptical about Deep Learning, because it wasn't "deterministic" (as they call it).
sents.zh: 我记得，在我刚进入自动驾驶领域的那段时间，一些大团队已经对深度学习持怀疑态度，因为它不是他们所说的“确定性”的。

paragraphs.en: We don't like Black Boxes, which is one of the main reasons End-To-End will struggle to get adopted. Is ChatGPT any better? I don't think so, and I would even say it's worse in many ways. However, LLMs are becoming more and more transparent, and the black box problem could eventually be solved.
paragraphs.zh: 我们不喜欢黑箱，这也是端到端方案难以获得采用的主要原因之一。ChatGPT 会更好吗？ 我不这么认为，我甚至认为它在很多方面更糟。 然而，大语言模型正变得越来越透明，黑箱问题最终可能被解决。

sents.en: We don't like Black Boxes, which is one of the main reasons End-To-End will struggle to get adopted. Is ChatGPT any better?
sents.zh: 我们不喜欢黑箱，这也是端到端方案难以获得采用的主要原因之一。ChatGPT 会更好吗？

sents.en: I don't think so, and I would even say it's worse in many ways.
sents.zh: 我不这么认为，我甚至认为它在很多方面更糟。

sents.en: However, LLMs are becoming more and more transparent, and the black box problem could eventually be solved.
sents.zh: 然而，大语言模型正变得越来越透明，黑箱问题最终可能被解决。

paragraphs.en: To answer the question "Can we trust them?"... it's very early in the research, and I'm not sure someone has really used them "online" — meaning « live », in a car, on the streets, rather than in a headquarter just for training or image generation purpose. I would definitely picture a Grok model on a Tesla someday just for Q&A purposes. So for now, I will give you my coward and safe answer...
paragraphs.zh: 要回答“我们能信任它们吗”这个问题……研究还处于非常早期的阶段，我不确定是否有人真正在“线上”使用过它们——也就是“实时”使用，比如在汽车里、在街道上，而不是仅仅在总部用于训练或图像生成。 我完全可以设想有朝一日在特斯拉上使用 Grok 模型，仅用于问答目的。 所以目前，我会给你一个胆怯而保守的回答……

sents.en: I would definitely picture a Grok model on a Tesla someday just for Q&A purposes.
sents.zh: 我完全可以设想有朝一日在特斯拉上使用 Grok 模型，仅用于问答目的。

sents.en: So for now, I will give you my coward and safe answer...
sents.zh: 所以目前，我会给你一个胆怯而保守的回答……
